rationale: No displayed earlier directive plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template. C14 is closest factually because it concerns the same Arkansas school-integration dispute and the same federal district-court order, but it is a short personal telegram and lacks the child's statutory findings, obstruction-of-justice formulation, finding that ordinary judicial enforcement is impracticable, and command to cease, desist, and disperse. C18 shares constitutional-rights language but concerns civil-rights policy generally and has no parallel operative machinery. C01 shares only standard proclamation form and execution boilerplate.

shared_material.child_excerpt: orders of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Arkansas with respect to matters relating to enrollment and attendance at public schools
shared_material.parent_excerpt: school integration recommended by the Little Rock School Board and ordered by the United States District Court
shared_material.explanation: C14 describes the same underlying controversy and court order, but this factual overlap does not amount to a reusable drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: denial of the equal protection of the laws secured by the Constitution of the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: assuring to all citizens equality under our Constitution and under the laws
shared_material.explanation: C18 has broad conceptual overlap concerning constitutional equality, but the wording and operative purpose are materially different.

shared_material.explanation: C01 contains identical proclamation boilerplate, which is routine and insufficient to establish a drafting-template relationship.
